name: clone()
description: Creates a new thread or process with fine-grained control over what resources are shared between parent and child. Unlike fork(), clone() accepts a bitmask of CLONE_* flags that determine whether the child shares the parent's address space, file descriptors, signal handlers, and more. It is the underlying primitive used by pthreads and container runtimes.
signature: int clone(int (*fn)(void *), void *child_stack, int flags, void *arg, ...)

main_flow.title: User Space — clone() call with CLONE_* flags
main_flow.description: The user-space program calls clone() directly or through the pthreads library (pthread_create). The caller provides a function pointer, a child stack pointer, and a bitmask of CLONE_* flags. The C library wrapper places the syscall number in %rax and the flags in %rdi, then executes the syscall instruction to enter the kernel.

detail_nodes.title: glibc clone() wrapper
detail_nodes.description: The glibc clone() wrapper sets up the child stack with the function pointer and argument, then invokes the syscall with the CLONE_* flags. For pthread_create, the wrapper additionally sets CLONE_VM | CLONE_FS | CLONE_FILES | CLONE_SIGHAND | CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_SYSVSEM | CLONE_SETTLS | CLONE_PARENT_SETTID | CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID.

detail_nodes.title: syscall instruction
detail_nodes.description: The syscall instruction atomically saves %rip and %rflags, switches to ring 0, and loads the kernel stack pointer from the TSS. Control jumps to the system_call entry point in entry_64.S. The syscall number for clone on x86-64 is 56.

source_ref.snippet:
ENTRY(system_call)
  SWAPGS_UNSAFE_STACK
  movq %rsp, PER_CPU_VAR(old_rsp)
  movq PER_CPU_VAR(kernel_stack),%rsp

detail_nodes.title: CLONE_* flags bitfield
detail_nodes.description: The clone_flags parameter is a bitmask controlling resource sharing. Key flags: CLONE_VM (share address space), CLONE_FS (share chroot/cwd), CLONE_FILES (share fd table), CLONE_SIGHAND (share signal handlers), CLONE_THREAD (same thread group), CLONE_NEWNS (new mount namespace). A plain fork() is equivalent to clone(SIGCHLD) with no sharing flags.

main_flow.title: Kernel Entry — sys_clone → do_fork() with flags
main_flow.description: The kernel's syscall dispatch routes NR_clone to sys_clone(), which is defined in kernel/fork.c (or architecture-specific stubs). sys_clone() validates the child stack pointer, copies the flags from user space, and calls do_fork() passing the CLONE_* flags. do_fork() is the shared entry point for fork(), vfork(), and clone().

detail_nodes.title: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(clone, ...)
detail_nodes.description: sys_clone() on x86-64 is defined via SYSCALL_DEFINE5 in kernel/fork.c. It receives the clone_flags, child_stack pointer, parent_tidptr, child_tidptr, and TLS pointer from registers. It validates that child_stack is non-NULL (required for clone, unlike fork), then calls do_fork().

detail_nodes.title: do_fork() — shared fork/clone entry
detail_nodes.description: do_fork() is the architecture-independent entry point for all process creation in Linux. It validates clone_flags for illegal combinations (e.g., CLONE_THREAD without CLONE_SIGHAND), then calls copy_process() to create the new task_struct. After copy_process(), it calls wake_up_new_task() to schedule the child.

detail_nodes.title: clone_flags validation
detail_nodes.description: do_fork() validates the clone_flags bitmask before proceeding. Certain flag combinations are illegal: CLONE_THREAD requires CLONE_SIGHAND; CLONE_SIGHAND requires CLONE_VM. If an invalid combination is detected, do_fork() returns -EINVAL immediately without allocating any resources.

main_flow.title: copy_process — dup_task_struct → thread_struct init
main_flow.description: copy_process() is the heart of clone: it calls dup_task_struct() to allocate a new task_struct and kernel stack, then conditionally copies or shares each process resource based on the CLONE_* flags. For threads (CLONE_THREAD), the child shares the parent's PID namespace and thread group ID.

detail_nodes.title: copy_process() orchestration
detail_nodes.description: copy_process() in kernel/fork.c validates flags, calls dup_task_struct() to create the child task_struct, then proceeds to copy each subsystem conditionally based on clone_flags. For CLONE_THREAD, the child gets the same tgid as the parent (same thread group).

source_ref.snippet:
static struct task_struct *copy_process(unsigned long clone_flags,
  unsigned long stack_start,
  struct pt_regs *regs,
  unsigned long stack_size,
  int __user *child_tidptr,
  struct pid *pid)

detail_nodes.title: dup_task_struct() — new task_struct + kernel stack
detail_nodes.description: dup_task_struct() allocates a new task_struct with alloc_task_struct() and an 8KB kernel stack with alloc_thread_info(). It copies the parent's task_struct wholesale, then sets up the thread_info pointer to the new stack. The child's kernel stack is a fresh allocation.

detail_nodes.title: thread_struct initialization
detail_nodes.description: copy_process() initializes the child's thread_struct with the user-provided stack pointer (for clone) or the parent's stack (for fork). The instruction pointer is set to ret_from_fork. For clone with CLONE_SETTLS, the thread-local storage descriptor is copied into the child's thread_struct.

detail_nodes.title: alloc_pid() — PID / TGID assignment
detail_nodes.description: alloc_pid() assigns a new PID from the global idr tree. For CLONE_THREAD, the child shares the parent's tgid (thread group ID) but gets its own unique PID. For a plain clone() without CLONE_THREAD, both PID and TGID are new, making it a new process.

main_flow.title: Shared mm — copy_mm with CLONE_VM flag
main_flow.description: copy_mm() checks CLONE_VM: if set (threads, containers), the child shares the parent's mm_struct and increments its reference count instead of creating a new one. Without CLONE_VM, dup_mm() allocates a new mm_struct and sets up copy-on-write page tables, just like fork().

detail_nodes.title: copy_mm() — CLONE_VM path
detail_nodes.description: When CLONE_VM is set, copy_mm() simply increments the reference count of the parent's mm_struct and assigns it to the child. Both parent and child now point to the same mm_struct, meaning they share the entire virtual address space including heap, stack mappings, and all memory mappings.

detail_nodes.title: mm_struct reference counting
detail_nodes.description: The mm_struct has two reference counters: mm_users counts the number of processes sharing this mm (incremented by CLONE_VM), and mm_count counts the number of references to the mm_struct itself (including from core dumpers and swap-out code). When mm_users drops to zero, the mm is freed.

detail_nodes.title: dup_mm() — without CLONE_VM
detail_nodes.description: When CLONE_VM is not set, copy_mm() calls dup_mm() to allocate a new mm_struct. It copies all VMAs via dup_mmap() and walks page tables to set up copy-on-write, identical to fork(). This is the path taken by container processes that want their own address space.

detail_nodes.title: copy_files / copy_sighand with CLONE flags
detail_nodes.description: Similar to copy_mm, copy_files() checks CLONE_FILES: if set, the child shares the parent's files_struct. copy_sighand() checks CLONE_SIGHAND: if set, the child shares the parent's sighand_struct. copy_fs() checks CLONE_FS for sharing cwd/root/umask. Each uses reference counting when sharing.

main_flow.title: Wake — wake_up_new_task → runqueue enqueue
main_flow.description: After copy_process() completes, do_fork() calls wake_up_new_task() to integrate the child into the scheduler. The child is marked TASK_RUNNING and enqueued on the CPU's CFS runqueue. For threads (CLONE_THREAD), the child shares the parent's signal group and thread group, so signals sent to the tgid are delivered to all threads.

detail_nodes.title: wake_up_new_task() — enqueue on runqueue
detail_nodes.description: wake_up_new_task() acquires the runqueue lock, calls activate_task() to insert the child's sched_entity into the CFS red-black tree, and sets the task state to TASK_RUNNING. For threads (CLONE_THREAD), the child is added to the parent's thread group list.

detail_nodes.title: Thread group linkage (CLONE_THREAD)
detail_nodes.description: When CLONE_THREAD is set, copy_process() links the child into the parent's thread group via list_add_tail_rcu(&p->thread_group, &p->group_leader->thread_group). All threads in the group share the same tgid and signal_struct. The group_leader field points to the thread that created the group.

detail_nodes.title: sched_entity for threads
detail_nodes.description: For CLONE_THREAD tasks, the sched_entity is initialized with vruntime inherited from the parent to maintain fair scheduling within the thread group. All threads in a group compete for CPU time as a single scheduling entity from the perspective of the CFS scheduler.

main_flow.title: Return — parent gets PID/TID; child starts at fn(arg)
main_flow.description: do_fork() returns the child's PID to the parent. The child begins execution at ret_from_fork, which jumps to the user-provided function pointer with the argument on the child stack. For threads (CLONE_THREAD), getpid() returns the same tgid for all threads, while gettid() returns each thread's unique PID.

detail_nodes.title: Parent returns child PID/TID
detail_nodes.description: do_fork() returns the child's PID to the parent via task_pid_vnr(). If CLONE_PARENT_SETTID was specified, the child's TID is written to the parent_tidptr address in user space. The parent resumes execution after the clone() call.

detail_nodes.title: Child starts at user fn(arg)
detail_nodes.description: For clone(), the child's stack was pre-populated with the function pointer and argument by the glibc wrapper. When ret_from_fork returns to user space, the child executes the provided function with the argument. When the function returns, the child calls exit() automatically (handled by the glibc wrapper).

source_ref.snippet:
ENTRY(ret_from_fork)
  DEFAULT_FRAME
  push kernel_eflags(%rip)
  CFI_ADJUST_CFA_OFFSET 8
  popf
  CFI_ADJUST_CFA_OFFSET -8
  call schedule_tail

detail_nodes.title: CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID — futex wake on exit
detail_nodes.description: When CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID is set, the kernel stores the child_tidptr and performs a futex(FUTEX_WAKE) on that address when the child exits. This is how pthread_join() knows when a thread has terminated — it waits on the futex and is woken when the child clears its TID.
